sourceTitle: Official manufacturer research: Steelcase, Haworth and Herman Miller
summary: Added manufacturer-supported task-chair knowledge for Steelcase, Haworth and Herman Miller, verified their US headquarters, and recorded the user's judgments that they form the main competitor set and belong to the Grade A range. Product facts remain separate from competitive and tier judgments.

records.statement: Steelcase's task-chair portfolio includes Leap with LiveBack and Natural Glide, Gesture with 360-degree arms for technology-shaped postures, and Karman with a responsive hybrid suspension seat.
records.notes: Verify the exact local configuration, warranty, pricing, availability and certifications before recommending.

records.statement: Haworth's task-chair portfolio includes Fern with Wave Suspension and Zody with adjustable asymmetrical lumbar support; official product pages also publish model-level ergonomic and sustainability certifications.
records.notes: Certification, warranty and model specifications vary by market and configuration; verify for the project location.

records.statement: Herman Miller's performance seating includes Aeron in three sizes with 8Z Pellicle and optional PostureFit SL, Embody for pressure distribution and supported movement, and Sayl with an unframed 3D Intelligent suspension back.
records.notes: Verify local warranty coverage, dealer support, configuration, lead time and commercial terms.

records.statement: Compare Steelcase, Haworth and Herman Miller at model and configuration level—not by brand name alone—using user fit, adjustability, body-size coverage, task pattern, materials, verified certifications, warranty and dealer support, lead time, installed cost and after-sales service.
records.notes: This is a comparison method, not a brand preference or hard rule. A user trial and project-specific evidence can change the advice.

records.statement: Steelcase, Haworth and Herman Miller are US-based workplace-furniture brands with headquarters in Grand Rapids, Holland and Zeeland, Michigan, respectively.
records.notes: Headquarters locations are verified from each manufacturer's official contact or company page.

records.statement: In the user's current competitive context, Steelcase, Haworth and Herman Miller are the three main US-based competitors to track.
records.notes: User-provided competitive judgment. Revalidate the active competitor set for each geography, opportunity and scope; do not treat it as a universal market fact.

records.statement: Classify Steelcase, Haworth and Herman Miller as Grade A brands in the current portfolio and competitor range.
records.notes: User-defined Grade A classification. Use it for premium-tier comparisons, but revalidate model fit, specification, local support, lead time and commercial terms for each opportunity.

summary: Added a reusable stakeholder framework for workplace-project pursuits. It separates importance from influence, distinguishes formal authority from informal influence, and links every key stakeholder to a project decision, evidence need and ethical engagement action.

records.statement: Stakeholder importance and influence are different: importance reflects how necessary their needs are to project success, while influence reflects their power to control decisions, resources, implementation or other people's actions.
records.notes: A high-importance user may have limited approval authority; a high-influence sponsor may be less involved day to day.

records.statement: For each project, map every named stakeholder by formal decision power, informal influence, interest, attitude, impact, access and relationship strength; update the map when the project phase or stakeholder behavior changes.
records.notes: Attitude can often change through relevant evidence and engagement; power and formal authority may be harder to change.

records.statement: Test the decision path across the economic decision maker, executive sponsor, end-user champion, procurement, project manager, designer or consultant, facilities, finance, IT, ESG, legal and any gatekeeper or blocker. Record who recommends, specifies, approves, signs, pays, uses and can veto.
records.notes: These are candidate roles, not a fixed organization chart. One person may hold several roles and titles alone do not prove influence.

records.statement: Winning support requires role-specific evidence: business value for the economic decision maker, strategic fit for the sponsor, user outcomes and trials for end users, compliance and comparability for procurement, delivery control for the project manager, design integrity for consultants, and risk, service and lifecycle evidence for operational stakeholders.
records.notes: Engage through relevant value and transparent evidence; never use manipulation, hidden inducements or unsupported claims.

records.statement: Prioritize high-power, high-interest stakeholders for close engagement; keep high-power, lower-interest stakeholders satisfied; keep high-interest, lower-power stakeholders informed and involved; monitor lower-power, lower-interest stakeholders for changes.
records.notes: Do not ignore a low-interest stakeholder with veto authority; their interest can rise suddenly.

records.statement: Before selecting product or price, connect the Win Objective to the real decision coalition: identify whose support is necessary, what each person must believe, which conflicts remain, and what new evidence could change the recommendation.
records.notes: The objective is not to pressure a decision maker; it is to build an evidence-backed coalition that can support a successful project outcome.

sourceTitle: ERGOVN brand portfolio and bid-positioning map
summary: Collected ERGOVN's publicly listed maker network, selected product anchors, project scopes and delivery capabilities. Added a strategic map for using the portfolio against Grade A US competitors without claiming unsupported one-to-one equivalence.

records.statement: ERGOVN publicly lists 17 makers: Zenith, Humanscale, Wilkhahn, Andreu World, Framery, HOLMRIS B8, HAY, Milliken, Teknion, Markant, Lamex, Arper, Actiforce, Wintech, Proffice, Artifort and Network++.
records.notes: Treat this as the public maker network as of 8 September 2026. Confirm representation status, territory, availability and authorization before each bid.

records.statement: ERGOVN highlights these selected product anchors: Humanscale Freedom task chair, HAY Result multi-use chair, Framery One Lounge acoustic pod, HOLMRIS B8 Neighborhood setting, Zenith Precinct Pod focus workstation and Wilkhahn Graph conference table.
records.notes: These examples demonstrate use cases; they are not the complete product range.

records.statement: ERGOVN positions itself for Office, Education and Hospitality projects across Vietnam and APAC, with public reference categories including office workspace, acoustic pods, education settings, carpet tile, ergonomic workplace and furniture settings.
records.notes: Project references on the site identify categories and makers but do not by themselves prove suitability for a new opportunity.

records.statement: ERGOVN describes an end-to-end offer covering strategic consultation, sourcing and consultation, project management, supply-chain management, supply and installation, organized around insight, specification and delivery.
records.notes: Use these as claimed public capabilities; validate the delivery plan, resources and evidence for the specific bid.

records.statement: Use the ERGOVN maker network as a scope portfolio: ergonomic and task seating; workstations and workplace systems; acoustic privacy; conference and collaboration; design-led ancillary furniture; flooring; height-adjustable components; and locally supported value-engineering options. Build the bid around the strongest verified combination for the project rather than forcing one maker across every scope.
records.notes: This grouping is a strategic interpretation of the public maker network. Verify each maker's exact product coverage and local commercial position.

records.statement: Against Grade A US competitors Steelcase, Haworth and Herman Miller, ERGOVN's core bid position should emphasize multi-brand freedom, fit-for-scope specification, Vietnam/APAC insight, design-team collaboration, budget balancing, supply-chain control, installation and after-sales execution—then prove product-level equivalence or advantage with compliant specifications, samples, trials, warranty, lead time and total installed cost.
records.notes: Do not claim that a listed brand is automatically equivalent to a competitor. Compare exact models, configurations, certifications, warranty, service and project evidence.

records.statement: Before using the portfolio in a bid, confirm the decision maker's success criteria, specified or incumbent brand, approved-equal rules, stakeholder influence map, user trial requirements, local stock and lead time, warranty responsibility, installation capacity, lifecycle service, price position and switching risk.
records.notes: These unknowns can materially change the recommended maker, scope and commercial scenario.

sourceTitle: Flokk and HOLMRIS B8 portfolio and competition review
summary: Added official-source knowledge on Flokk as a design-led multi-brand workplace-furniture group and HOLMRIS B8 as a multi-brand design, project-delivery and circular-service partner. Added a bid comparison method without creating an unsupported portfolio preference or universal competitor classification.

records.statement: Flokk is an Oslo-headquartered family of specialized, design-led workplace-furniture brands. Its current official About page lists HÅG, Giroflex, Offecct, Connection, RH, Profim, 9to5 Seating, Stylex, VIA Seating, Malmstolen and Spec.
records.notes: Treat the list as current to 9 September 2026. Verify the active brand portfolio, local distribution, territory and model availability before a bid.

records.statement: Flokk positions its group around professional and public-space furniture, with roots in Scandinavian task seating and capabilities spanning chairs, sofas, benches, stools and spatial solutions. Its sustainable-design method emphasizes lower weight, fewer components, material choice, long life and design for disassembly.
records.notes: Product sustainability, certification, recycled-content and warranty claims must be verified at exact model and market level.

records.statement: When Flokk appears in a bid, identify the exact Flokk brand and model instead of comparing against the group name alone. Test ergonomics, application fit, verified environmental data and certifications, warranty, local service, lead time, trial results and total installed cost.
records.notes: This is a comparison method, not a claim that Flokk is always a direct competitor or Grade A equivalent.

records.statement: HOLMRIS B8 describes itself as a furniture-industry sales and design company with roots dating to 1914, more than 350 furniture experts, access to its own designs and products from more than 1,000 suppliers, and specialist activity across Office, Learning, Care and Hospitality.
records.notes: Verify current geographic coverage, supplier authorization and delivery resources for the opportunity.

records.statement: HOLMRIS B8 publicly offers furniture advice, project management, delivery and assembly, relocation, storage, repairs and upgrades, furniture care, registration, take-back, climate data, resale, donation and sorting. This extends its proposition beyond new-product supply.
records.notes: Use these as public company claims and validate the exact contractual scope, geography, documentation and service-level commitment.

records.statement: Treat HOLMRIS B8 as a service-led, multi-brand project integrator when it is active in an opportunity. ERGOVN should compare design-team access, breadth of sourcing, project control, local and APAC execution, installation, lifecycle care, circular services, climate documentation and total delivered value—not furniture price alone.
records.notes: Opportunity-specific judgment only. Do not assume direct competition, identical territory or equivalent capability without evidence.

records.statement: Do not treat Flokk and HOLMRIS B8 as the same competitor type: Flokk is principally a manufacturer group with differentiated product brands, while HOLMRIS B8 presents a sourcing, design, delivery and circular-service platform. The win strategy and evidence plan should match the role each one plays in the bid.
records.notes: Revalidate the actual contracting and distribution structure for every geography and opportunity.

sourceTitle: Vietnam import supply-chain, shipping and tax framework
summary: Added a landed-cost and supply-chain decision framework for furniture and project goods imported to Vietnam from China, the EU and Australia. Tariff advice stays conditional on HS classification, originating status, proof of origin, customs value and current regulations; no blanket country tax rate was created.

records.statement: Goods entering Vietnam require an HS classification. The applicable import tariff depends on the product's HS code, origin and the tariff schedule that can legally be claimed; Vietnam's National Trade Repository provides MFN and preferential FTA tariff tables plus rules-of-origin information.
records.notes: Never estimate duty from country name or product description alone. Confirm the current Vietnam HS code and tariff at declaration.

records.statement: For Vietnam imports, customs value is based on the actual value payable up to the first import border gate under the applicable customs-valuation rules. Import VAT is calculated on the dutiable value plus import duty and any applicable additional import, excise or environmental taxes.
records.notes: The VAT and duty rates remain HS-code- and policy-specific. Reconfirm them with the customs broker before quoting.

records.statement: Qualifying China-origin goods may access preferential treatment under ACFTA or RCEP when the product-specific origin rule and documentary requirements are met. ACFTA uses Certificate of Origin Form E; shipping from China does not by itself prove Chinese origin.
records.notes: Compare the eligible ACFTA, RCEP and MFN rates for the exact HS line, then retain the valid proof of origin and transport documents.

records.statement: Qualifying EU-origin goods may receive EVFTA tariff treatment when the agreement's product-specific origin rules and proof-of-origin requirements are satisfied. Depending on the case, proof can include a certificate of origin or an eligible origin declaration or statement.
records.notes: An EU invoice or EU shipping port is not sufficient by itself. Confirm originating status and the acceptable proof for the shipment.

records.statement: Qualifying Australia-origin goods may access preferential treatment under AANZFTA or RCEP when the applicable product-specific rule of origin is met. AANZFTA claims require compliant origin documentation, including the applicable Certificate of Origin process.
records.notes: Compare the eligible AANZFTA, RCEP and MFN rates for the exact HS line and verify current certification procedures.

records.statement: Estimate landed project cost as product value plus origin handling and export charges, international freight, insurance, dutiable additions, import duty, non-recoverable taxes, customs brokerage, port and terminal charges, inspection, storage or demurrage exposure, inland delivery, installation handling and a documented risk reserve.
records.notes: Separate recoverable VAT from true project cost when the importing entity can legally claim input VAT. Finance and the customs broker must confirm treatment.

records.statement: Use different planning assumptions by origin: China often offers more regional routing and consolidation choices; EU cargo normally needs a longer ocean-planning horizon and stronger transshipment control; Australian routing depends heavily on origin port and sailing frequency. Obtain a current forwarder quote and carrier schedule for every bid.
records.notes: This is a planning pattern, not a promised transit time. Port pair, mode, season, equipment, consolidation and carrier schedule can change the result.

records.statement: Before shipping, align the purchase order, Incoterm, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, HS classification, proof of origin, product description, quantities, values and any permits or inspection requirements. Resolve discrepancies before cargo arrival.
records.notes: Late or inconsistent documents can delay clearance, lose preferential duty treatment and create storage or demurrage costs.

records.statement: A bid using imported goods should show a base landed cost and a risk-adjusted landed cost. Test freight volatility, foreign exchange, origin-document failure, customs reclassification, inspection, damage, delay, storage, demurrage and last-mile installation against project margin before P approves the price.
records.notes: Do not hide logistics contingency inside product cost. Keep assumptions visible and refresh them when the quote validity or shipping plan changes.
